card.title: QUEEN'S OWN

card.flavorText: The Queen’s Own Cameron Highlanders was a Scottish infantry regiment, renowned for its Highland heritage and service in British military campaigns from 1793 to 1961. During WWII the regiment’s battalions fought in every major theater. The 1st Battalion began the war in France with the British Expeditionary Force, endured the retreat and evacuation at Dunkirk, and then redeployed to Burma, where it played a vital role in the intense campaigns at Kohima, Mandalay, and the Irrawaddy River. The 2nd Battalion, stationed in North Africa at the war’s outbreak, fought in Operation Battleaxe before being captured at Tobruk. After reforming in the UK, they went on to serve in Tunisia, Italy, and Greece. The 4th Battalion, after being captured at Saint-Valéry-en-Caux in France, was reformed in the UK and helped rebuild the 2nd Battalion, with some members serving garrison duty in Bermuda. The 5th Battalion saw action at El Alamein, Sicily, Normandy, and in the pivotal battles of Caen, the Falaise Gap and the Bulge. The 7th Battalion transformed into a parachute unit. The regiment’s legacy also extended to the Australian 61st Battalion, which became the “Queensland Cameron Highlanders” and fought in the Pacific.
